::: {#sol-skip-zero-grad}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
stale_rule = SoftRule()
stale_optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(stale_rule.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
stale_grads, stale_cutoffs = [], []
for step in range(100):
    loss = nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy(stale_rule(ink_01), is_one)
    loss.backward()
    stale_grads.append(stale_rule.cutoff.grad.item())
    stale_optimizer.step()
    stale_cutoffs.append(stale_rule.cutoff.item())
theta_stale = stale_cutoffs[-1]
sides = np.sign(np.array(stale_cutoffs) - theta_module)
n_crossings = int(np.sum(sides[1:] != sides[:-1]))
print(theta_stale, stale_grads[:2], min(stale_cutoffs), max(stale_cutoffs), n_crossings)
```

The cutoff ends at `r sprintf("%.4f", py$theta_stale)`,
not at `r sprintf("%.4f", py$theta_module)`.
`loss.backward()` adds each new gradient to the one already in `.grad`,
so without `optimizer.zero_grad()` the gradient used at each step is the sum of the gradients of every step so far.
The first step is the same as in @exm-training-step,
with `.grad` at `r sprintf("%.4f", py$stale_grads[[1]])`,
but at the second step `.grad` is `r sprintf("%.4f", py$stale_grads[[2]])`,
the first step's gradient plus the second's.
The sum stays negative after the cutoff passes the lowest point of $\emprisk$,
until enough positive slopes beyond it have been added,
so the cutoff overshoots and swings back:
over the 100 steps it ranges from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(unlist(py$stale_cutoffs)))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(unlist(py$stale_cutoffs)))`,
and crosses `r sprintf("%.4f", py$theta_module)` `r py$n_crossings` times.
PyTorch adds rather than replaces so that a gradient can be built up over several backward passes,
for example over pieces of a batch too large to fit in memory at once.

:::
